chunks: From him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

key_terms.أَبَانٌ: Aban ibn Tammam, a key narrator
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَيَابَةَ: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.فَضَالَةَ: Fudaylah ibn Yasar, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it, indicating this narration confirms a previously mentioned ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the skins of dead animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar* reaffirms the prohibition of consuming or utilizing the skins of *meat al-haywan* (animals that died without proper slaughter) through a chain leading to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It serves as a corroborative report (*muthal*) within the chapter on the impurity of dead animal hides, emphasizing the juristic consensus on their ritual impurity (*najasa*) in Shia fiqh.
